$comment: THE BRIEF. Written by /design-system:init from the interview; read by every other command, by the token build, by the lint rules and by the inventory site. Record the WHY in each rationale field — in two years someone will ask why the team is on this stack and the answer should be in the repo, not in a Slack thread.
name: acme-ui

rationale.primitives: Base UI 1.x — actively maintained, render-prop composition, and the default the shadcn CLI now targets.
rationale.componentLayer: Own the code. Brand consistency is the reason this system exists, so a vendor's visual opinions are a cost, not a saving.
rationale.cssSystem: Tailwind v4 — @theme makes every token a CSS custom property, which is the shortest path from the DTCG source to something components can use.
rationale.motion: Motion — this is product UI, not a brand site; AnimatePresence covers the exit animations CSS cannot.
rationale.icons: Lucide — 24px grid, per-icon imports, and the default the surrounding ecosystem assumes.
rationale.$comment: If the constraint pass overrode an interview answer (e.g. componentLayer heroui forcing cssSystem tailwind), say so here: 'Tailwind v4 — implied by HeroUI, which peer-requires tailwindcss>=4.' resolved:true above asserts that pass ran.

contrast.$comment: enforce:true makes a failing pair fail the BUILD. Contrast as a CI gate rather than a review comment is the highest-leverage accessibility decision available — it makes the failure impossible to merge rather than easy to miss.

typography.$comment: 1.200 (minor third) is the safe default for product UI. 1.333+ is editorial.

distribution.$comment: mode: in-repo | workspace | private-npm | public-npm. In-repo is right for a single app — a package adds a version boundary and a lag between change and use. It earns its keep at 2+ consumers.

conventions.$comment2: render (Base UI) | asChild (Radix) | as. Pick ONE — mixed conventions are the most common cause of 'why does this component not compose'.

ai.$comment: Emits AGENTS.md from the registry so coding agents get the same single source of truth the docs site renders. Without it, agents invent component names and hardcode hexes.
